title: 'Tensei Kizoku, Kantei Skill de Nariagaru 3rd Season' Unveils Additional Cast, Third Promo for Fujimiya Family Arc
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Miraijin A 's Tensei Kizoku, Kantei Skill de Nariagaru: Jakushou Ryouchi wo Uketsuida node, Yuushuu na Jinzai wo Fuyashiteitara, Saikyou Ryouchi ni Natteta ( As a Reincarnated Aristocrat, I'll Use My Appraisal Skill to Rise in the World ) light novel unveiled additional cast, a third key visual (pictured), and the third promotional video for the third season on Monday. The new arc is scheduled to premiere on November 1 at 11:30 p.m. on CBC and TBS' 28-station "Agaru Anime" programming block.

Cast Rikuya Fujimiya: Toshiya Miyata ( Ore wa Seikan Kokka no Akutoku Ryoushu! ) Maika Fujimiya: Mariya Ise ( Made in Abyss ) Takao Fujimiya: Takaki Ootomari ( Hibi wa Sugiredo Meshi Umashi )

Takao Kato ( Pandora Hearts ) is directing the anime at GeyeG Pictures , with Hiroaki Matsushima ( Arifureta Shokugyou de Sekai Saikyou 2nd Season episode director) serving as assistant director. Daisuke Oohigashi ( Fate/Strange Fake ) is handling the series composition. Yuuko Yahiro ( Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai: Tensai-tachi no Renai Zunousen ) is designing the characters. Kujira Yumemi ( Lv2 kara Cheat datta Motoyuusha Kouho no Mattari Isekai Life ) is composing the music.

Produced by studio MOTHER , the first season aired in 12-episode in Spring 2024, followed by the second season in Fall 2024. Crunchyroll streamed the anime with subtitles in multiple languages and an English dub.

Miraijin A began penning the novel on the Shousetsuka ni Narou website in October 2019. Kodansha published the first volume with illustrations by JIMMY under its K Ranobe Books imprint in July 2020. The ninth volume went on sale on June 2, with the tenth volume scheduled for a December 2 release.

Natsumi Inoue began drawing a manga adaptation on the Magazine pocket app in June 2020. Kodansha published the 21th volume on June 9.

Kodansha USA licensed both the manga and light novel in English in November 2021 and March 2022, respectively. The 14th manga volume went on sale on April 21. The seventh light novel volume was published in November 2025.

PV 3

title: Goddess of Victory: Nikke Game Gets New Manga Adaptation
content:
The official X (formerly Twitter ) account for Kadokawa 's Dengeki Maoh magazine announced on Saturday that SHIFT UP 's Goddess of Victory: Nikke game will receive a new official manga adaptation by Yokoshima Penguin this winter to celebrate the franchise's fourth anniversary. The manga will focus on the Goddess squad as the main characters.

Yokoshima Penguin has contributed to Nikke manga anthologies in the past.

The game previously inspired a slice-of-life manga by Kio Utsusumi titled Goddess of Victory: Nikke Sweet Encounter .

Goddess of Victory: Nikke combines gacha card collecting with shooter-style gameplay. Publisher Level Infinite launched the game globally on iOS and Android devices on November 4, 2022. The game also launched a PC version in February 2023 with single account login and cross-play with the mobile version. As Level Infinite describes the story, "players lead a squad of android soldiers called Nikke, the last hope for reclaiming the overworld from a vicious race of aliens called Raptures who have forced humanity underground."

The game has featured collaborations with Chainsaw Man , NieR: Automata , Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- , and Evangelion .

A-1 Pictures animated a special video for the game's "Old Tales" event in 2024.

title: New Live-Action Street Fighter Film Drops to #4 in the U.S.
content:
Legendary Entertainment 's new live-action film of CAPCOM 's Street Fighter game series dropped from #1 to #4 in the U.S. box office in its second weekend. The film earned an estimated US$8,600,000 in the October 23-25 weekend, a 72.1% drop from its opening weekend earnings. The film has earned a estimated cumulative total of US$46,938,634 in the United States, and US$79,638,634 worldwide.

The film continued its engagement in Imax theaters, where it earned US$1.8 million or 21% of its second U.S. weekend total. Its cumulative Imax total is now US$12 million. Its 10-day total in the United States is 25% less than Mortal Kombat 2's 10-day total.

The film opened on October 16, ranking #1 in the United States, and earning US$30,775,377 in its first three days.

The film opened at #8 in Japan, earning 134,019,900 yen (about US$853,900) in its first three days.

Paramount Pictures describes the story:

Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu ( Andrew Koji ) and Ken Masters ( Noah Centineo ) are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li ( Callina Liang ) recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don't, it's GAME OVER!

The cast includes:

• Andrew Koji as Ryu

• Noah Centineo as Ken

• Rayna Vallandingham as Juli

• Orville Peck as Vega

• Mel Jarnson as Cammy

• Jason Momoa as Blanka

• Eric André as Don Sauvage

• David Dastmalchian as M. Bison

• Cody Rhodes as Guile

• Callina Liang as Chun-Li

• Andrew Schulz as Dan Hibiki

• Roman Reigns as Akuma

• Alex Volkanovski as Joe

• Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson as Balrog

• Olivier Richters as Zangief

• Hirooki Gotō as E. Honda

• Vidyut Jammwal as Dhalsim

Paramount Pictures and Legendary signed a multi-year distribution deal in December, with Paramount Pictures distributing Legendary Entertainment films worldwide except China (Legendary East handles distribution in China). Street Fighter is the first film to be distributed under the new deal. Legendary Entertainment acquired the film and television rights to Street Fighter in April 2023, and will work with CAPCOM on future projects.

Sony Pictures was previously slated to distribute the film. When the film was still slated to be distributed by Sony Pictures , the film was planned to open on March 20, 2026, but Sony removed the film from its release calendar in March 2025.

Kitao Sakurai (The Eric André Show, Bad Trip) directed the film's shoot in Australia, which started in August 2025. Brothers Danny and Michael Philippou were initially slated to direct the film, but left the film to focus on making their Bring Her Back film.

The game series inspired a live-action film in 1994 starring Jean-Claude Van Damme , Raúl Juliá, Ming-Na Wen , Damian Chapa , Kylie Minogue , and Wes Studi . Hyde Park Entertainment produced a separate spinoff titled Street Fighter : The Legend of Chun-Li starring Kristin Kreuk in 2009.

Machinima produced the Street Fighter : Assassin's Fist and Street Fighter : Resurrection live-action series . Machinima released the first series on its YouTube channel in May 2014, and Funimation licensed the series for release in North America. Funimation released the series on Blu-ray Disc in October 2014. Machinima released the second series on Verizon's go90 streaming service in March-April 2016. A Street Fighter : World Warrior television series was originally planned in 2018.

Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie adapted CAPCOM 's video game Super Street Fighter II in 1994. Discotek Media released the film on DVD in December 2015, and on Blu-ray Disc in October 2016. The franchise has also inspired several other anime and animated series.

The Street Fighter 6 fighting game launched in June 2023 for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam . CAPCOM released the game on Nintendo Switch 2 in June 2025 as a launch title. The Street Fighter 6 Years 1-2 Fighters Edition version also launched on the same day.
author: ANN

title: Patlabor EZY Anime Gets Novelization in 2027
content:
The " Fantasia Bunko Grand Fan Appreciation Festival 2026 Online" event on Sunday announced that a novelization of the Patlabor EZY anime project will launch next year. Toshihiko Tsukiji ( Maburaho , Kämpfer ) is writing the novelization, and the Patlabor franchise 's longtime character designer Akemi Takada is drawing the cover illustration.

The Patlabor EZY anime consists of eight episodes, and is opening theatrically as three films. "File 1" opened on May 15, and "File 2" opened on August 14. The first two films feature the anime's first six episodes in an omnibus format with stand-alone stories. "File 3" will open on March 5 and will contain the last two episodes which tell a two-part story.

The story is now set in the 2030s, with Japan facing increased labor shortage and increased automation via AI. Labors, the piloted mecha that was once considered cutting edge technology for manual labor, has become just another part of life, with piloted Labors themselves increasingly being replaced with autonomous robots. SV-2's job of preventing Labor crimes remains the same even in this age, as they use a tuned-up version of their original SV-98 Ingrams.

Shigeru Chiba is reprising his role as Shigeo Shiba in the anime. Chiba has played the role since the original anime's debut almost 40 years ago.

Yutaka Izubuchi ( Patlabor mechanical designer) is directing the anime at J.C. Staff . Kazunori Itō ( Patlabor the Mobile Police ) is writing the script. Masami Yuuki ( Patlabor creator) is designing the characters. Takamitsu Satou ( Lostorage incited WIXOSS ) is the chief animation director and character designer. Kenji Kawai ( Patlabor ) is composing the music. GENCO representative director Tarō Maki ( Patlabor the Mobile Police , Nodame Cantabile , Millennium Actress ) is producing. GAZEN is handling CG production. The HEADGEAR group is credited for the original story.

GENCO revealed the Patlabor EZY anime project with a booth at the MIFA film market at Annecy International Animation Film Festival in 2017. The pilot for the project debuted in August 2022, and then played alongside a one-week 35th anniversary revival screening run of Patlabor: The Movie that started on September 20, 2024. Izubuchi directed the video.

The Patlabor franchise 's original concept of police officers piloting robotic mecha (patrol labors or "Patlabors") was developed by HEADGEAR , a group consisting of director Mamoru Oshii ( Ghost in the Shell , Sky Crawlers ), script writer Kazunori Itō ( .hack , Dirty Pair ), mecha designer Yutaka Izubuchi ( Eureka Seven , Mobile Suit Gundam franchise ), character designer Akemi Takada ( Kimagure Orange Road , Urusei Yatsura , Fancy Lala ), and manga creator Masami Yuuki ( Birdy the Mighty ). The franchise spawned two original video anime, a television anime series, and three anime films. The last anime film, Patlabor WXIII , opened in theaters in Japan in 2002.

title: Rainy Day Serenade Manga Gets Spinoff Series in November
content:
The December issue of Kodansha 's Kiss magazine announced on Friday that Haruka Kawachi 's Rainy Day Serenade ( Namidaame to Serenade ) manga will receive a spinoff manga series titled Namidaame to Serenade : Gaiden ( Rainy Day Serenade Side Story) in the magazine's next issue on November 25.

The story follows a heartbroken Kikunoshin who encounters a sudden commotion at the Fuji Sakura cafe he frequents.

Kawachi launched the original manga in Kodansha 's Kiss magazine in 2014, and ended it in November 2025. Kodansha shipped the manga's 14th and final compiled book volume in February. Kodansha USA Publishing licensed the manga, and is releasing the manga in two-in-one omnibus volumes.

The series is inspiring an anime adaptation in 2027.

Kawachi launched the Musashino Rondo manga in Shodensha 's Feel Young magazine in 2020. Shodensha published the manga's first compiled book volume in September 2021, and the fifth volume in July 2025. The series inspired a live-action series in April 2025.

Kawachi's Natsuyuki Rendezvous manga received an anime adaptation on Fuji TV 's Noitamina block in 2012, the same year the manga ended.

Kawachi launched the Request o Yoroshiku ( Welcome Your Request ) manga in Feel Young in September 2014 and ended it in 2019. Shodensha published the manga's fifth and final volume in 2020.

JManga published Kawachi's Sekine's Love manga in English.

title: 24 Years Ago, This Shonen Anime Left Fans Hanging (& Its Reboot Couldn’t Save It)
content:
Shaman King may not have received the anime adaptation it deserved, but it remains one of the most beloved series of all time. There’s no denying that the 1990s were a revolutionary era in the anime and manga industry, especially when it came to Shonen series. Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine, in particular, witnessed the rise and fall of many classics. Some of the series, such as Dragon Ball, One Piece, Naruto , and many more, etched their names in history thanks to their exceptional stories. On the other hand, many unique series, such as Shaman King , eventually became forgotten despite their initial popularity.

Written and illustrated by Hiroyuki Takei , Shaman King began serialization in Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine before Studio Xebec released an anime adaptation in 2001. However, only a year later, on September 25th, 2002, the anime reached its conclusion before fully adapting the story. The original anime was discontinued due to several reasons, but that might have cost the franchise its shot at success. Even more than 24 years later, the original anime is the only adaptation that never completed the story. While a reboot was released in 2021, it did more harm than good, dashing any possibility of the series becoming more popular.

Shaman King ‘s Original Anime Wasn’t Perfect, But it Deserved a Longer Run

The original anime was a massive success, but it still had one crucial flaw. Anime series back in the 1990s and 2000s were released in long-running format, which severely affected the pacing and animation quality. Not to mention that because the manga which they were based on were also serialized weekly, these long-running anime caught up with the manga sooner than expected. There’s no denying that many great shows suffered due to this common practice, which is why the seasonal anime series that became popular in the 2010s and 2020s have been so well-received.

Regardless, the original anime ended in 2002 after it caught up with the manga, but it never returned with a sequel. While a major reason behind it was the production and budget, we also can’t ignore the manga’s rocky serialization. By the time the manga was in the final arc, Takei was dealing with several health issues and burnout. The story came to an abrupt end in 2004, but he later revived the series in special editions, which is why the reboot managed to adapt the entire story.

The slow pacing in the original anime isn’t surprising considering it was a common practice back in the day to stop the anime from catching up to the manga while adding as few fillers as possible. However, the biggest issue was the inconsistent animation quality, which couldn’t attract new viewers. Additionally, the original anime deviated from the canon source during the end, which ruined the adaptation even more. Despite its shortcomings, the original anime was significantly better than the reboot , which is why it deserved to adapt the entire story.

Shaman King ‘s Reboot Couldn’t Save the Franchise

The anime reboot was released in 2021 , and it adapted the entire story. However, despite the anticipation, the reboot was a major flop since it was considered a disappointment among fans due to the rushed pacing and lackluster animation quality. Instead of adapting the manga faithfully, which fans wanted all along, the studio compressed almost 300 chapters into 52 episodes . This caused the reboot to skip several important character-building moments, and even the relationship between them felt hollow and vague. Despite being a modern production, the anime suffered significantly due to production issues and a poor budget.

Fans couldn’t ignore these problems since the static frames and below-average visuals could only mean that the studio failed to invest as much money in the project as required. Additionally, the reboot couldn’t capture the nostalgic charm of the 2001 anime, which reflected the soul of the story. It’s not uncommon for reboots to end up becoming an even bigger disappointment than the original. However, since the anime already got a second shot and the ending is already adapted, there’s little to no chance that Shaman King will ever get an adaptation it deserves.

Do you think Shaman King ’s reboot did justice to the original anime, or did it fail to recapture what made the story so special? Let us know in the comments below.

It’s not uncommon for reboots to end up becoming an even bigger disappointment than the original. However, since the anime already got a second shot and the ending is already adapted, there’s little to no chance that Shaman King will ever get an adaptation it deserves.
Do you think Shaman King ’s reboot did justice to the original anime, or did it fail to recapture what made the story so special? Let us know in the comments below.

title: 3 Darkest Anime of Fall 2026 That You Shouldn’t Miss
content:
It is only a little over two months before 2026 comes to an end, and the current Fall season marks the final anime season of the year, featuring numerous new releases. This year has been intriguing for the anime industry, with a variety of anime airing from the start. However, the ones that have stood out the most are those featuring darker elements.

The year began with anime such as Sentenced to Be a Hero and Jujutsu Kaisen , with subsequent seasons bringing even more. Now, the Fall season is living up to the trend established throughout the year, with three particularly dark anime that live up to the hype and are ones that fans shouldn’t miss.

3) The Apothecary Diaries Season 3

Of all the anime airing this season, The Apothecary Diaries is arguably the only returning series with some of the darkest tropes, as it has always been built around dark themes. The third season starts differently, with the main characters outside the castle as new events begin to unfold. It reveals that the threats Maomao and Jinshi will have to face far exceed anything they have overcome before.

The series doesn’t incorporate these dark elements through heavy fantastical concepts but instead relies on grounded storytelling, making its darker themes resonate even more with fans. Moreover, it gradually executes these elements, unveiling the threads of dark mysteries as the characters uncover them alongside viewers, creating a sense of self-discovery. With its return for Season 3, The Apothecary Diaries has once again highlighted why it is one of the best historical drama anime of all time, with dark elements that feel just right.

2) The Vermilion Mask

For an anime to be dark, it doesn’t necessarily have to fall into the seinen category, which has more freedom in depicting mature themes. The Vermilion Mask proves this. On the surface, it has all the elements of a shonen series, but its darker tropes and tragic foundations make it the kind of modern shonen anime that fans have come to love. At its core is the protagonist, Peru, whose tragic past and journey toward healing form the heart of the story.

However, while fans might expect Peru’s journey to become slightly easier, the second episode adds even more gravity to his struggles , making him an even more tragic protagonist. Meanwhile, the third episode goes a step further, introducing an intriguing twist that stuns viewers and reveals how much darker his journey is than they might have expected. If The Vermilion Mask continues on this trajectory, it could emerge as Fall 2026’s darkest anime.

1) Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2

The return of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners , the 2022 Anime of the Year, with its second season was undoubtedly one of the most anticipated anime releases of the year. The first season is arguably one of the darkest and most emotional journeys to follow across its 10 episodes, as David navigates life in Night City in pursuit of a different future. Every element of the series is built on tragic foundations that are enough to make viewers cry. Although the second season introduces new characters, it follows the same narrative approach.

With a protagonist who has experienced a downfall and is now searching for a new purpose in life, the story finds its direction through his efforts to protect someone else. It is a profound narrative structure that draws viewers in effortlessly, while more characters with their own tragic stories are gradually introduced. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 captures the same vibe as the first season and is undoubtedly one of the darkest anime not just of Fall 2026 but of the entire year, now available to watch on Netflix.

title: 36 Years Ago, Dragon Ball Z Introduced a Fan-Favorite Character Toriyama Didn’t Create
content:
Dragon Ball is one of the oldest and most iconic anime and manga franchises of all time, especially within the Shonen demographic. It goes without saying that the creator, Akira Toriyama , is responsible for creating the majority of the characters. However, not all of the characters known among fans were from the manga. As the animation studio behind such a popular series, Toei Animation has contributed significantly to the franchise’s popularity. The anime adaptation not only became a massive success in Japan, but it eventually turned into a global sensation not long after it became popular in the West. Not only did the animation studio adapt the main story from the manga, but it also created several spin-offs, sequels, and prequels that weren’t part of the original story by Toriyama.

During the 1990s, the animators and directors would often take liberties to create new characters and even transformations from scratch that eventually became fan-favorites. Goku’s father, Bardock, is one of the most iconic characters in the franchis e, introduced in the television special, Dragon Ball Z: Bardock – The Father of Goku . It was broadcast on October 17th, 1990 in Japan, and even 36 years later, the character is still just as loved as he was before.

Goku’s Father Was Introduced in a Non-Canon Episode of Dragon Ball

Katsuyoshi Nakatsuru, one of the most renowned animators and character designers behind the anime, was primarily responsible for designing Bardock along with the rest of the team. The special episode serves as a prequel to the original story, following Goku’s father before Frieza destroyed Planet Vegeta, the home of the Saiyan warriors. The 1990 episode takes place 12 years before the events of the main story, following Bardock and his crew of Saiyans who used to go on missions for Frieza. The Saiyans were doing Frieza’s bidding for a while, making them the perfect labor force for them.

Due to their immense strength, they would easily destroy planets and make them ready for sale to the highest bidder. However, it didn’t take long before Frieza turned his back on the Saiyans. He always feared that a Super Saiyan would emerge from someone among them and defeat him with the help of that legendary power. After his infant son, Kakarot, was sent to the planet, Bardock also fought on the front lines to stop Frieza from destroying the planet. However, not a single Saiyan was a match against the villain’s overwhelming power. The original episode was a massive success, and Bardock eventually became a fan-favorite character .

Bardock Eventually Became an Iconic Dragon Ball Character

Several years after the episode’s premiere, Toriyama briefly included him in the main story, honoring the character’s efforts in trying to save his son and his people. The 1990 episode revealed that Goku was sent to Earth to destroy it on a mission. The context was more aligned with the original story, but things changed in Dragon Ball Super when Bardock officially became a canon character . A brief flashback in Chapter 77 showed that Bardock knew that something tragic would take place on the planet, which is why he sent his infant son to Earth so the low power levels there would keep the baby hidden from Frieza. This quality completely changed the core of the character, and whether it worked out for the best or not depends on individual preferences.

Toei’s version of the character is more ruthless, cold, and emotionally distant, perfectly fitting for an anti-hero. However, Toriyama made Bardock more caring and soft, who sent his son away to protect him from the impending destruction. While one is morally gray and complex, the other version of this character is a tragic hero. Despite the significant differences, both versions of Bardock are just as beloved, with the Toei one being slightly more favorable among fans. The quality that makes Bardock intriguing is that he doesn’t fit the standard criteria of a “hero.”

Saiyans weren’t a peaceful race, and they were known for being bloodthirsty and always craving more power. Bardock was no different since he was introduced as a ruthless Saiyan warrior who takes pride in battle and conquest, just like everyone else. This is why the original anime from 1990 makes more sense given the context and the background of Planet Vegeta. After gaining the ability to see the future, he realizes the Saiyans are on the verge of extinction and that Frieza will betray them. He did everything he could to save his race, but even he knew it was a losing battle.

What makes Bardock such an iconic character in the Dragon Ball franchise, and do you think his story deserves more anime adaptations? Let us know in the comments!

title: 3 Anime to Watch on Prime Video This October
content:
October 2026 is closer to its end than ever, which means Halloween is right around the corner. The spooky season also brought back several exciting anime sequels such as The Apothecary Diaries and Black Clover. While the anime sequels and even the new debuts are more than exciting enough, not many of them fit the Halloween vibe. Lucky for us, platforms such as Crunchyroll, Hulu, Netflix, and more don’t fall short of exciting anime series for every season and mood. Prime Video is one such platform that has been venturing deep into the anime world for quite some time now.

Thanks to that, the library is expanding each season with critically acclaimed shows such as Nippon Sangoku , The Ghost in the Shell (reboot), and many more series that aren’t streaming anywhere else. While there are only a few days before this month wraps up, there’s more than enough time to catch up with these exciting anime shows. While they’re not conventionally Halloween-centric shows, they do have enough dark vibes and spookiness to be the perfect show you need for the season.

3) Banana Fish

MAPPA, the same studio behind Jujutsu Kaisen and Attack on Titan Final Season, released Banana Fish in 2018, when it was still gaining a foothold in the industry. However, the anime was a huge success thanks to its exceptional story and gorgeous visuals. The story also follows sensitive themes, including psychological aspects that make it one of the darkest Shojo of all time. The story focuses on ruthless street gangs, human trafficking, exploitation, and all kinds of issues that are rarely seen within the Shojo demographic. Unlike fantasy stories, Banana Fish follows characters that are deeply human, which makes the suffering all the more excruciatingly painful. The anime is based on a 1985 manga written and illustrated by Akimi Yoshida, which has a more expansive story than MAPPA’s adaptation. Whether it’s the dark themes of the story or the fan-favorite Halloween episode, Banana Fish is a must-watch for everyone before the end of this month.

2) Tatsuki Fujimoto 17-26

Best known for creating acclaimed Shonen manga such as Chainsaw Man and Fire Punch , Tatsuki Fujimoto is one of the most renowned creators in recent years. Aside from his critically acclaimed series, he has released several one-shots over his decade-long career. In November 2025, six animation studios banded together in November 2025 to release an eight-episode-long series titled Tatsuki Fujimoto 17-26 . Each episode of the series was produced by a different animation studio, including P.A. Works, Studio Kafka, and more. The project aimed to adapt the forgotten one-shots by the celebrated creator and introduce them to fans all across the globe. The eight episodes of the series follow different stories and characters, ranging from sci-fi to love stories, and many more genres. Additionally, each episode offers a thought-provoking story that lingers for a while as viewers are immersed in Fujimoto’sartistic world. The anime episodes aren’t traditionally horror jump scares, but what makes them truly perfect for Halloween is their weird, dark, and psychological themes.

1) Dororo

Based on Osamu Tezuka’s 1967 manga , Dororo is a reboot of the 1969 anime, Dororo to Hyakkimaru . The anime was released in 2019, but it never received as much popularity as it deserves. While not a complete flop, the series still deserves so much more attention, but it couldn’t catch viewers’ eyes since it doesn’t have flashy animation or Shonen battles. The story follows the unimaginable struggles faced by the protagonist, yet he continues to fight each day just to earn the right to exist in a world where he was abandoned from the day he was born. Since his father, a samurai lord, sacrificed him to the 12 demons, Hyakkimaru was born without limbs, a nose, eyes, ears, or even skin, yet he still survived due to his mother’s prayers. He was saved by a kind man who created prosthetics and weapons, allowing him to grow up and embark on a journey to defeat the demons and reclaim what he had lost.

Do you like our picks – or have an anime you’d like to recommend that is available exclusively on Prime Video? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Crunchyroll’s Darkest Anime of Fall 2026 Unveils Its True Story With a Twist No One Expected
content:
The new episodes of all currently airing anime on Crunchyroll this Fall 2026 are being released weekly, and arguably the darkest anime of the season has just incorporated a twist that no one saw coming. Darker tropes have become a trend in modern anime, with more and more series, especially shonen, following this format. However, seinen anime have long embraced this approach, so it is no surprise that the currently airing seinen anime, The Vermilion Mask , is emerging as one of the darkest of the year. The anime explores the trauma of its main character, who is on a journey of redemption.

Peru has been living with guilt ever since he wielded the restricted power that resulted in the deaths of his master, Gaston Roux, and the other apprentices. He vowed to eliminate the masks his master had created because they were too powerful and no one else should have to go through the same ordeal. The second episode showcased this resolve, as Peru remained determined to continue his journey even after losing his right arm . However, the latest episode, the third of the series, introduced an unexpected twist by revealing that Gaston, his master, is alive, along with an intriguing detail that could define what the entire series is about.

Crunchyroll’s The Vermilion Mask Just Blew Everyone’s Mind With an Intriguing Twist and Detail

The Vermilion Mask ‘s third episode , as it comes to an end, features Sonarue looking at the list of masks that Peru intends to eliminate. Among them is the Mask of the Warrior God, which is ranked at level four out of five. This is a surprising detail, as everyone expected it to be the highest level, but apparently, there is only one level-five mask. This mask is half-broken and has no name or description, so Peru names it “The Vermilion Mask” based on its appearance. While this detail is revealed, a bus passing by Peru and the others reveals that one of its passengers is Gaston, Peru’s master, whom he thought he had killed, or someone who looks exactly like him.

This is an intriguing detail that essentially changes the entire narrative. Peru is on a journey to destroy Gaston’s masks because he fears what they are capable of. However, as the creator of these masks, Gaston himself is an intriguing character, and the assumption that he died because of one of his own creations is now difficult to accept. It suggests that Gaston could be the mastermind behind something much bigger, potentially rendering Peru’s journey obsolete. While there are many possibilities for what this actually means, it is clear that Gaston’s appearance in the latest episode has shifted the narrative beyond simply destroying masks.

The story could now focus on unveiling the dark mysteries behind the origins of these masks and why the Vermilion Mask is the only one ranked at level five. The Vermilion Mask continues to surprise fans with intriguing details as more episodes are released, just as it did with the introduction of Mok Sharib, the new character who joined the group. All these elements reinforce the idea that the anime’s narrative is built on tragic and mysterious foundations, making it one of Fall 2026’s darkest anime currently airing on Crunchyroll . If it maintains this momentum, it could emerge as the darkest anime of 2026 as well.
